item.description:
0.11.3

Two things you told us about the grey suggestion.

  • The grey text sat on top of the character you had just typed. Its position comes from the terminal cursor, but right after a keystroke the cursor has not moved yet — the device has to echo the character first. We drew one column early, and the overlap followed you across the line.
  • One press of ← silenced suggestions for the rest of the line. Any arrow key used to mean "this line is beyond us". Now ← and → are counted: we stay quiet while the cursor is away from the end and pick up again when it returns. End brings it back too.
  • We still stand down where we genuinely cannot follow — typing in the middle of a line, ⌃← , Home and ↑↓. A suggestion placed on a line we have misread is worse than no suggestion.
